title: Weighted-Average Cost
description: Use average inventory cost to calculate COGS and ending inventory.
html:
What is weighted-average cost?

Instead of assigning specific old or new costs to units sold, the weighted-average method uses an average cost per unit.

Basic formula

Average Cost Per Unit = Total Cost of Goods Available ÷ Total Units Available

Example

Assume a company has the following inventory:

100 units × $10 $1,000
100 units × $14 $1,400
200 units available $2,400

Step 1 — Calculate average cost

$2,400 ÷ 200 units = $12 per unit

Step 2 — Calculate COGS

Suppose the company sells 150 units.

150 × $12 = $1,800 COGS

Step 3 — Calculate ending inventory

The company has 50 units remaining.

50 × $12 = $600 Ending Inventory

Check your work

COGS + Ending Inventory should equal total cost of goods available for sale.

$1,800 + $600 = $2,400

FIFO vs LIFO vs Weighted Average

FIFO

Oldest costs flow to COGS first.

LIFO

Newest costs flow to COGS first.

Weighted Average

Costs are averaged together.

Remember

Weighted average smooths differences between different purchase costs.

quiz.prompt: A company has 100 units costing $8 each and 100 units costing $12 each. What is the weighted-average cost per unit?
quiz.explanation: Total cost is $2,000 and total units are 200. $2,000 ÷ 200 = $10 per unit.
